label: Classical attributes defined from Dei Filius ch. 1, sufficiency derived from named bridges
summary: Item 4 (third part) of the modal spine's next investigations: the stage-two sufficiency premise STMT-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-SUFFICE had no derivation and targeted the primitive signature field HasClassicalAttributes. The field stays primitive and undefined (changing the skeleton would break frozen Challenges); a DEFINED predicate DeiFiliusAttributes (TruthCore/Causality/DeiFiliusAttributeField.lean, definition edcfac86) gives the attributes of Dei Filius ch. 1 as recorded in claim VATICAN-I-DEI-FILIUS-CH1-ONE-TRUE-LIVING-GOD (DS 3001, goodness from DS 3002) in a typed reading, each a typed predicate or an explicitly identified primitive with stated meaning and obligations. No source was newly read for the readings; analyst formulations, attribution deferred. The typed reading is weaker than the text for creator (no creation from nothing), 'infinite in intellect and will' (the conjunction), substance (untyped; IsSpiritual alone is also satisfied by prime matter or accidents) and 'exalted above all' (not exceeded in being); STRONGER for goodness (IsSupremelyGood includes causing every perfection of everything else, beyond DS 3002's 'bonitate sua', which names the motive of creation; 'creator' is contained in it by definition, not substantively derived); and a DIFFERENT reading for 'really and essentially distinct from the world' (RemoteFromAll; incomparable with the text: the anti-pantheist content of DS 3001 and canons DS 3023-3024 is untyped, and a Spinozist God satisfies RemoteFromAll). 'True' is kept as the IsGod predicate. INTERPRETATION FORK of the primitive field (disambiguation 2cbf40b4, CLASSICAL_FIELD): Root.lean documents the field as 'intended to group simplicity, perfection, goodness, infinity, immutability, eternity, unity, intellect and will', exactly the nine (CLASSICAL_FIELD_1); the Dei Filius motivation is in ClassicalAttributesSuffice's docstring, DEF-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-BUNDLE and the claim (CLASSICAL_FIELD_2, the full typed list). On the nine-reading the old premise is close to analytic, the field interpretation follows at once and the bridges do no work for sufficiency; on the full-list reading the bridges carry the warrant. LIVING (disambiguation 1f2d3b9b): the Dei Filius living conjunct is the timeless primitive Primitives.Lives (LIVING_1, definition f91f5056). The corpus already has a typed time-indexed route (SelfOperationLife, result PURE-ACT-LIVES-FROM-SELF-OPERATION: life as self-operation, derived for pure act as life present at some time of a duration frame), recorded as the sibling reading LIVING_2 (LivesSomeTime); not reused, because it adds a duration frame and a primitive Operates and identifying it with the timeless sense would merge senses (invariant 7); composing them needs an explicit bridge. Verified, zero axioms (specs/dei-filius-attribute-field.toml): (1) nineGiveDeiFilius: at an arbitrary being, the nine give every typed Dei Filius attribute from seven new open bridges (intellect gives life; causing the being of all gives lordship, immensity and being a component of nothing; infinity gives incomprehensibility; perfection with intellect gives beatitude; excess in being is excess in act) and three existing premises (STMT-INFINITE-ACT-HAS-INFINITE-POWER for almighty; goodness-is-actuality and the q.3 a.7 matter-form clause for exalted and spiritual). Almighty is active power and immutability the absence of passive potency, so no sense clash (DISAMB-POTENCY linked). (2) classicalAttributesSufficeOfDeiFilius: the old premise from the restated one plus the field interpretation FieldFromDeiFilius, its first derivation; this relocates part of its warrant into a stipulation about an undefined primitive, it does not discharge it. (3) deiFiliusRoot: the registered join-to-stage-two composition (result 57213a13) reused, without its sufficiency premise, on a signature whose field is trivial; the root then has every typed Dei Filius attribute from five of the new bridges plus the existing infinite-power premise. (4) classicalRootOfDeiFiliusRoot: the old endpoint from the new one plus the field interpretation. (5) controls: nonvacuity; for nine of the ten premises of (1) a one-being interpretation where it alone fails, the nine hold and some typed attribute fails; the field interpretation holds while the old premise fails (strictness). The lemma fieldOfSuffice (old premise gives the field interpretation) is lake-checked but deliberately not registered (as an argument it would close a support cycle that hides the field interpretation from the frontier), so the strictness claim is not Comparator-verified on its weak side; no strengthens relation, since the strength order is for strength forks of one ambiguous proposition and its backing result would recreate the cycle. OBJECTION AUDIT (substantive objection standard): no substantive objection identified to the field interpretation or to six of the bridges. NO-COMPONENT BRIDGE: q.3 a.8 itself (passage AQUINAS-ST-I-Q3-A8, read 2026-11-12) reports three contrary positions: God as world-soul (via Augustine, De civ. Dei VII), God as the formal principle of all things (the Amalricians) and God as prime matter (David of Dinant), and obj. 1 cites Dionysius ('the being of all is the deity above being; the being of all enters each composite'). The Amalrician position and obj. 1 have a clear target and mechanism: they can grant that God causes the being of all and deny the consequent, God's giving being being his being the formal being of things. Aquinas replies that the efficient cause is not numerically one with the form of what it makes, that the first agent acts primarily and per se while a component does not, that no component is simply first, and (ad 1) that deity is the being of all effectively and exemplarily, not by essence. Independent justification on file: none; the positions are attested only through Aquinas's report (no Amalrician, David of Dinant or Dionysian source is pinned), so this is a named formal alternative with a stated mechanism, not a substantive objection; Spinoza remains an unread lead and in any case satisfies RemoteFromAll. EXCESS-IN-ACT BRIDGE: an interpretation dependence from the quarta via's own picture of more and less in one perfection: with a binary InAct it holds only if respects separate grades; this bears on the reading, not the truth, and the bridge is unused at the root. WARRANT AUDIT: no claim states any new bridge or the field interpretation; each bridge cites the Summa article giving its reason (q.18 a.3, q.13 a.7, q.8 a.1-2, q.12 a.7, q.26 a.1, q.3 a.8, q.4 a.2) without a pinned reading; the field interpretation is a stipulation about a primitive on the full-list reading, strictly weaker than the old premise. No premise is established. Under the full-list reading the warrant gap of the sufficiency premise is the field interpretation plus seven named bridges (five at the root) and the existing infinite-power premise; under the nine-reading it is the near-analytic old premise itself.
blocker: Not blocked. Next tests: give typed content to the five primitives (life without change for an immutable being, or an explicit bridge from LIVING_2; dominion; presence to effects and place; created intellects and degrees of knowability; beatitude), so that their bridges can be derived or fail; type a world term (numerical non-identity with the world as a whole, the anti-pantheist content of DS 3001 and DS 3023-3024) and creation from nothing; decide whether the respects of InAct separate grades of being (DISAMB-IN-ACT); weigh the CLASSICAL_FIELD fork (which reading the downstream uses of the primitive field need); read the cited Summa articles, and any Amalrician or Dionysian source, into pinned claims only if a bridge's warrant becomes the selected question.
